title: Logs
description: Every log line the fleet ships, and the line rate that says whether anything is arriving at all. Filter by machine, container, level and a substring. The log panel shows each line's message, parsing a JSON or key=value line at query time; the stored lines are unchanged. Every panel that serves an alert evaluates that alert's own expression once per refresh and colours its value by that alert's threshold, so what you see here is the number the page was computed from.

panels.title: Total lines/min
panels.description: Is anything arriving at all? One line, every selected stream summed — the transport canary, and the panel a "no lines in the last six hours" page lands on. A flat zero here while the fleet is otherwise healthy means the shipping path is down, not that the fleet went quiet. Context panel: no alert evaluates this expression, so it carries no threshold line — the silence rules and the count each of them computes are in the silence-rule table at the lower right. Counted per minute; the shipping paths here are low-volume by design, so a healthy total is a small number.

panels.title: Error rules — ERROR lines in each rule's window
panels.description: What the four error rules count right now. Each row is one rule's own expression, evaluated once per refresh as the rule evaluates it: the ERROR and CRITICAL lines of the capture daemons, of the ops machine and of the trading engine in the last fifteen minutes, up to five messages each with the message in the row's name, and of the archive-pull loop. A row turns red at one line, where its rule fires, with no pending period; a quiet rule reads 0. The archive-pull row carries no machine filter because that container name exists only on the NAS — the ops machine's own pull loop ships under a different name. The lines themselves are in the log panel below.

targets.expr: topk(5, sum by (host, container, level, msg) (count_over_time({host=~"zcrypto|zcrypto-red", container="capture", level=~"ERROR|CRITICAL"} | json message="message" | drop __error__, __error_details__ | label_format msg=`{{ if .message }}{{ printf "%.200s" .message }}{{ else }}{{ printf "%.200s" __line__ }}{{ end }}` [15m]))) or on() vector(0)

topk(5, sum by (host, container, level, msg) (count_over_time({host="ops", container=~"alloy|liquidations|zcrypto-.*", level=~"ERROR|CRITICAL"} | json message="message" | drop __error__, __error_details__ | label_format msg=`{{ if .message }}{{ printf "%.200s" .message }}{{ else }}{{ printf "%.200s" __line__ }}{{ end }}` [15m]))) or on() vector(0)
sum by (host) (count_over_time({container="archive-pull", level=~"ERROR|CRITICAL"} [15m])) or on() vector(0)

topk(5, sum by (host, container, level, msg) (count_over_time({host="zcrypto", container="engine", level=~"ERROR|CRITICAL"} | json message="message" | drop __error__, __error_details__ | label_format msg=`{{ if .message }}{{ printf "%.200s" .message }}{{ else }}{{ printf "%.200s" __line__ }}{{ end }}` [15m]))) or on() vector(0)

panels.title: Silence rules — lines in each rule's window
panels.description: Which stream went quiet? Each row is one silence rule's own expression, evaluated once per refresh as the rule evaluates it: six hours for the two capture daemons, for the trading engine, for the shipping agent's own stream on the ops machine and for the liquidations poller; twenty-six hours for the scheduled ops units, one row per unit, and for the ops journal transport; three hours for the archive-pull success line. A row turns red below one line, where its rule fires, with no pending period. Any count from one up is healthy: the trading engine logs in bursts on its four-hourly cycle, so its count sits far below the capture daemons' and is still healthy, dead only at 0. Container names are not symmetric across machines — the archive-pull loop is `archive-pull` on the NAS and `zcrypto-archive-pull` on the ops machine — and the archive-pull success row carries no machine filter because that container name exists only on the NAS. A zero and a stream that never existed read the same here; the last-line table above tells them apart.

targets.expr: sum by (host) (count_over_time({host="zcrypto", container="capture", level=~".+"} [6h])) or on() vector(0)
sum by (host) (count_over_time({host="zcrypto-red", container="capture", level=~".+"} [6h])) or on() vector(0)
sum by (host) (count_over_time({host="ops", container="alloy", level=~".+"} [6h])) or on() vector(0)
targets.legendFormat: dead-man · shipping agent's own stream, ops (6h)

targets.expr: sum by (host) (count_over_time({host="ops", container="liquidations", level=~".+"} [6h])) or on() vector(0)
sum by (host, container) (count_over_time({host="ops", container=~"zcrypto-.*", level=~".+"} |~ "^\\S+ \\[\\S+\\] - " [26h])) or on() vector(0)
sum by (host) (count_over_time({host="ops", container="zcrypto-archive-pull"} [26h])) or on() vector(0)
sum by (host) (count_over_time({host="zcrypto", container="engine", level=~".+"} [6h])) or on() vector(0)

panels.title: Last line seen — per stream
panels.description: A rate of zero and a stream that never existed render identically on a graph; this table tells them apart. One row per stream that has shipped at least one line in the last twenty-six hours — the widest window any log rule evaluates — carrying the wall-clock time of that line. A row present with an old timestamp is a stream that has gone quiet. **A row missing while other rows are present** is a stream already past every rule's patience; streams that exist on only one machine are expected to be missing from the other, and the edge machine ships metrics only, so it never appears here at all. **An entirely empty table means something different, and never that the whole fleet went silent.** Unless the pickers are narrowed to the edge machine alone, or to a container none of the selected machines runs, no rows at all means this panel's own query failed — a broken panel, not a verdict. Read the line rate to its left before you treat anything as an outage: it answers the same question through a different query, and if it shows lines arriving then this table is the thing that is wrong. Context panel, carrying no threshold of its own — the silence rules' pages land on the table beneath it, which holds each rule's own count.

targets.expr: max by (host, container) (max_over_time({host=~"$host", container=~"$container"} | label_format seen=`{{ unixEpoch __timestamp__ }}` | unwrap seen [26h])) * 1000

panels.title: Logs — $container / $level
panels.description: Every line, newest first, shown as its message, parsed here at query time; the stored line is unchanged. A JSON line — the capture daemon, the trading engine and the liquidations poller push one JSON object per record — shows its message, with any stack trace beneath it. A key=value line — the shipping agent's own and the monitoring node's services' — shows its message, after its logger or its source location where it names one, and the error it carries. Any other line, the scheduled jobs' and the other services' own, shows as it was collected. Level is a real stream label on every path, so filtering and colouring work the same way for all of them. Expand a row to see the fields parsed out of it: a JSON line's logger, source file and line and its structured fields, a key=value line's logger, source location and error.

targets.expr: {host=~"$host", container=~"$container", level=~"$level"} |= "$search" | json jmessage="message", jexception="exception", jmsg="msg", jlogger="logger", jfile="file", jline="line", jextra="extra" | logfmt lmsg="msg", llogger="logger", lcaller="caller", lerror="error", lerr="err" | drop __error__, __error_details__ | line_format "{{ if .jmessage }}{{ .jmessage }}{{ if .jexception }}\n{{ .jexception }}{{ end }}{{ else if .jmsg }}{{ .jmsg }}{{ else if .lmsg }}{{ if .llogger }}{{ .llogger }} - {{ else if .lcaller }}[{{ .lcaller }}] - {{ end }}{{ .lmsg }}{{ if .lerror }}: {{ .lerror }}{{ else if .lerr }}: {{ .lerr }}{{ end }}{{ else }}{{ __line__ }}{{ end }}"

list.name: host
list.label: Host
list.query: Capture primary : zcrypto, Capture secondary : zcrypto-red, Ops : ops, NAS : nas, Edge : zaccess, Cache 1 : zcrypto-valkey1, Cache 2 : zcrypto-valkey2, Cache 3 : zcrypto-valkey3, Monitor : zcrypto-mon, Dead-man : zcrypto-hc
list.description: Which machines the panels below select. All expands to the pinned machines joined into one matcher — the option list is the pin, so a stray label value cannot appear here. The edge machine ships metrics only and no log lines at all, so selecting it on its own empties every panel on this board by construction rather than by fault. The monitor and dead-man machines ship their log lines to the monitor's own Loki alone, so on Grafana Cloud selecting either on its own empties this board the same way. This list is a second place to edit when a machine joins the fleet.

list.name: container
list.label: Container
list.description: Container or unit that produced the line. The names are not symmetric across machines: the archive-pull loop appears in this list as `archive-pull` on the NAS and as `zcrypto-archive-pull` on the ops machine, so picking one of them silently blanks the other machine. Leave it on All unless you are chasing a single stream.

list.name: level
list.label: Level
list.description: Log level, carried as a real stream label on both paths — set by the shipping agent for the streams it collects, and by the daemon itself for the ones that push straight to the log store. Multi-select; All stays a match-anything pattern on purpose, so lines that carry no level label at all — the pull loop's own shell output — still appear.

list.name: search
list.label: Search
list.description: Case-sensitive substring filter on the log line (leave empty for all).
